title: Zuckerbergs Endorse Tom Holland's BERO Beer on Instagram Live
htmlContent:
Mark Zuckerberg's tenth-anniversary Smokin' Meats broadcaston Instagram Live had ribs, sausage, and an AI agent watching the smoker. It also had an unexpected product endorsement. Midway through the cook, Zuckerberg and his younger sister, Arielle Zuckerberg, cracked open cans of BERO, the premium non-alcoholic beer co-created by Tom Holland, and gave it a very public thumbs up.

"Have You Tried Spider-Man's New Beer?"

The moment started casually. Zuckerberg turned to his sister and asked, "Have you tried Spider-Man's new beer?"

Arielle's response was pure confusion:

"What?" "Tom Holland apparently has a new, uh, non-alcoholic beer," Zuckerberg explained. "It's pretty good."

Arielle didn't need much convincing.

"Oh, I would love to try some. Let's do it." "That's in the bag," Zuckerberg replied.

It is hard to imagine a better endorsement for a beverage brand than an unscripted recommendation from one of the most-watched tech founders in the world, delivered live to an audience tuning in for a nostalgia-fueled barbecue.

A Shared Tom Holland Fandom

Before the cans were even open, the siblings bonded over the actor himself.

"Okay, I'm a big Tom Holland fan," Arielle said. "Yeah, who isn't? Tom Holland's awesome," Zuckerberg answered.

Holland's star power is a big part of BERO's appeal. The actor co-founded the brand with CEO John Herman, and the company describes itself as "born in London, crafted in America, and enjoyed worldwide." The pitch is simple: a non-alcoholic beer that does not feel like a compromise, made for people who want to stay fully present in the moment.

The Snap Check

Then came the most charming bit of the segment. Arielle brought up something she had seen online.

"You know, I saw a reel yesterday of some dude in Australia who could tell what kind of beverage it was by the snap of the can opening." "Oh, really?" Zuckerberg asked.

Zuckerberg, never one to pass up an experiment, proposed a test on the spot:

"Let's do a snap check on that."

The cans cracked open, and the verdict came quickly.

"This is delicious," Arielle said. "It is good," Zuckerberg agreed. "Which one? Which flavor?"

Arielle had the Pils. Zuckerberg had picked up a different BERO flavor and gave it his own seal of approval:

"It's pretty good."

Why the Pils Matters

Arielle's pick is the brand's flagship. BERO's Kingston Golden Pils is an award-winning, crisp, European-style pilsner brewed for a clean, balanced finish. It is also the beer inside BERO's limited-edition Spider-Man cans, a collaboration with Sony Pictures tied to Spider-Man: Brand New Day.

The timing of the Zuckerbergs' shout-out could not have been better for the brand. The first run of Spider-Man cans, released in July alongside the film's theatrical premiere, sold out within two weeks and drove a 121% increase in site traffic, making it one of BERO's most successful limited releases to date. Starting October 8, a second limited run returned on berobrewing.com and exclusively at Topgolf venues, timed to the film's arrival on digital storefronts on October 6.

In other words, Mark Zuckerberg's question — "Have you tried Spider-Man's new beer?" — was more literal than it sounded. The cans currently on shelves feature collectible Spider-Man designs.

Non-Alcoholic, Fully In the Moment

BERO has worked hard to position itself not as the drink for people sitting things out, but as one for people who want to be part of the action.

"We didn't create BERO to be the beer people reach for when they're opting out. We created it for people who want to be fully in the moment," Herman said in announcing the Spider-Man re-release.<

That philosophy fits neatly with what played out on the live stream. Smokin' Meats has always been about Zuckerberg being casual and present in front of the camera, and a pair of siblings sharing a cold, alcohol-free beer by the grill is exactly the kind of moment BERO's marketing aims for. The brand has also built its presence around social settings, with partnerships like BERO x Barry's and the BERO Padel Classic, and now Topgolf as its exclusive on-premise retailer for the Spider-Man cans.

A Family Affair for the Anniversary

Arielle Zuckerberg, a venture investor, is not a regular fixture on her brother's streams, which made her appearance a fun bonus for viewers. The siblings' easy back-and-forth, from her confusion over "Spider-Man's new beer" to the impromptu snap test, gave the anniversary broadcast a warm, home-video feel that the original 2016 stream never quite had.

Ten years ago, Smokin' Meats was a meme. Today it is a tradition, complete with homegrown livestock, a Bluetooth-connected smoker managed by Meta's Muse AI agent, and now a celebrity-backed beverage making a cameo. Tom Holland didn't have to show up in person. With two Zuckerbergs vouching for his beer on Instagram Live, BERO got its own moment in the smoke.
excerpt: During Mark Zuckerberg's tenth-anniversary Smokin' Meats Instagram Live broadcast, he and his sister Arielle cracked open cans of Tom Holland's premium non-alcoholic BERO beer on camera, delivering an unscripted live endorsement for the celebrity-backed brand.
